claims.text: The target material is a multiphase eutectic high-entropy alloy containing BCC and sigma phases.
The phases in the target alloy can form protective oxide scales at elevated temperature.
Frictional heating during sliding promotes reaction with oxygen and formation of an oxide layer.
Cyclic shear stress during sliding fragments or spalls the protective oxide film.
Differences in mechanical response between microstructural constituents create heterogeneous deformation and localized stress concentrations.
Stress concentrations and oxide spallation are concentrated at phase boundaries.
Removal of the oxide film leaves the underlying phases unprotected and promotes further material loss.
Fragmented oxide and fractured hard particles act as abrasive debris, while stress accumulation at the interface promotes adhesive wear.
Wear at 600–800 °C can involve oxidative and adhesive mechanisms.
Oxide disruption exposes fresh surfaces that undergo accelerated oxidation because of differential oxidation kinetics between phases.
Oxide disruption creates localized, phase-dependent galvanic cells.
Localized galvanic corrosion accelerates corrosion at phase boundaries during sliding.
Combined wear and corrosion produce synergistic total degradation greater than that observed in either isolated wear or isolated corrosion.
Combined exposure increases the wear rate relative to the wear-only baseline.
Combined exposure increases corrosion current density or decreases passivation stability relative to the corrosion-only baseline.
An intact and stable protective oxide layer is maintained during the proposed wear-only baseline.
The accelerated coupled mechanism is significant only around 600–800 °C and under sustained cyclic wear.
At lower temperature or under less aggressive wear, the oxide remains sufficiently intact to suppress galvanic corrosion.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing wear-only, corrosion-only, and combined wear-corrosion conditions while measuring wear, oxide continuity, and electrochemical response.
Failure of the combined condition to exceed the sum of isolated wear and corrosion, or persistence of an effective continuous oxide, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that sliding-generated cyclic shear fragments the oxide film, whereas the wear-only baseline assumes that an intact and stable protective oxide is maintained under wear. No changed load, atmosphere, or other condition is specified to reconcile these statements.

The design requests identical environmental conditions for wear-only, corrosion-only, and combined tests, but a genuinely wear-only control must omit the corrosive exposure and a corrosion-only control must omit sliding. The intended matching variables therefore need to be stated more precisely.
